catalog_migration.reason: Regenerate the approved Chimney Swift plate to correct the page layout and exact field-mark grammar, and to ensure both short legs and tiny gripping feet originate anatomically from the ventral lower body and contact the vertical surface. The replacement refreshes the complete plate; all visible text, anatomy, ruler semantics, and composition were independently re-reviewed.

profile.behavior: An almost continuously aerial insectivore; flies rapidly with stiff, shallow wingbeats and clings rather than perches when at rest.
field_marks: Very long, narrow, strongly curved wings
Short, tapered tail with stiff, bristle-like tips
Dark gray-brown overall, with a slightly paler throat
Tiny feet; clings to vertical surfaces rather than perching
Very short, broad-based bill that is often hard to see
profile.habitat: Open airspace over a wide variety of terrain where flying insects are available; nests and roosts on enclosed vertical surfaces, including chimneys, cavities, caves, and similar structures.

sources.title: Chimney Swift Identification — All About Birds

findings: The primary specimen is a convincing Chimney Swift: one complete bird with one head and short bill, one visible eye, two folded wings, two legs with clinging feet, and a distinct short, tapered, bristle-tipped tail.
The two long lower projections now read as separate folded wings, while the shorter central feather group reads clearly as the tail; the detached wing and head are intentional supplementary studies.
Dark gray-brown plumage, slightly paler throat, slender body, long narrow wings, large dark eye, tiny feet, and vertical-clinging posture agree with the field references and direct sources.

All visible identification, habitat, behavior, field-mark, palette, and measurement text is legible and matches the proposed profile without material spelling, number, unit, duplication, omission, or word-order errors.
The body-length schematic increases correctly from 4.7 in (12 cm) at the bottom to 5.9 in (15 cm) at the top, agrees with the printed range, and is explicitly labeled “SCHEMATIC — NOT TO SCALE.”
The plate contains no place name, ZIP code, coordinates, map, or local-observation detail.

Direct sources confirm Chimney Swift, Chaetura pelagica, family Apodidae, the illustrated field marks and behavior, and the stated Cornell measurement ranges. Audubon independently corroborates the length and weight ranges and gives a broadly overlapping wingspan range.
